transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Jordan Li (Redwood SE); Liam O'Connor (Acme Platform); Priya Shah (Acme Security); Diego Morales (Acme Network)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: weekly POC check-in focused on networking/routing and runtime upgrade status for Redwood Private pilot in Acme VPC.
References: runbook v2 (https://s3.redwood/pilot/runbook-v2.pdf), internal benchmark sheet (link shared in chat).

Transcript Body:
[00:00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Liam: Liam here.
[00:00:08] Priya: Priya here.
[00:00:10] Diego: Diego on the net team.
[00:00:12] Jordan: Jordan from Redwood, thanks all.
[00:00:20] Maya: cool, agenda — short status, Jordan will cover runtime fix, Diego we'll go over peering/route questions, then next steps.
[00:00:35] Diego: quick note, we ran the connectivity test overnight, we're seeing intermittent egress failures to the model registry, sometimes times out at TLS handshake. looks asymmetric, maybe return path hitting the wrong NAT.
[00:00:50] Jordan: yeah that's consistent with what the logs show on the runtime side; connection established from instance but return RSTs or large TTL. seems like route for the response is not via the peering.
[00:01:05] Liam: to add context, we have two transit gateways and a pair of NAT gateways, one in each AZ, we suspect the TGW policy may be preferring the public path.
[00:01:18] Priya: also want to flag that audit logs need to land in our secure bucket with 7 year retention and we need KMS BYOK.
[00:01:26] Maya: noted, we'll include audit retention in the runbook. Jordan, runtime?
[00:01:30] Jordan: quick recap: last week's upgrade to runtime v2.3 introduced a kernel combo that is causing a quantized operator mismatch on the customer's GPU drivers. it's not a Redwood Privet problem — sorry — Redwood Private, but the deployed image uses cuX kernels that don't match their node image. so we built a patched image (v2.3.1-pilot) that falls back to CPU-safe paths for those ops and enables quantization-friendly kernels.
[00:01:55] Diego: will that affect latency significantly? our SLA target is 100ms p99 for short-generation paths.
[00:02:04] Jordan: minimal for the short paths; for long decode it's slightly higher but still within the pilot SLOs. the bigger hit if routing keeps dropping packets is failed handshakes which show as high latency or errors.
[00:02:18] Liam: ok, so network first, runtime second.
[00:02:22] Maya: action: Jordan will push the patched image to the registry and provide instructions to pull into our private ECR. Diego, can you confirm registry egress rules?
[00:02:32] Diego: currently outbound to s3 and mcr is allowed but we block some external repos. we need the exact hostnames and ports.
[00:02:40] Jordan: we'll provide a short allowlist: registry.redwood-inference.com:443, s3.amazonaws.com:443 (for model artifacts), and an IP range for the control plane. I will put them in the runbook.
[00:02:52] Priya: for KMS/BYOK, we need an IAM role that Redwood can assume for decrypt during startup, plus audit log write permissions. also looking for assurance on no plaintext keys written to disk.
[00:03:06] Jordan: standard pattern: we recommend an IAM role with sts:AssumeRole limited to instance profile scope and an encrypted SSM param for the key ARN. runtime doesn't persist plaintext keys. I'll document the flow.
[00:03:18] Maya: thanks. Diego, about the asymmetric routing, can you share the route table and TGW attachments?
[00:03:24] Diego: yes, I'll export the route table. one thing we found: the peering route to Redwood control plane is present but the return path from our TGW to the az NAT has a propagated route that prefers the internet gateway for that CIDR.
[00:03:39] Liam: so packets from our nodes go to Redwood via peering but responses come back via internet because of propagation?
[00:03:44] Jordan: that would explain the TLS resets we're seeing in the logs.
[00:03:47] Diego: i'll get the exact route entries.
[00:03:50] Priya: i also want to note compliance question: do you have SOC2 attestation docs for the private control plane?
[00:03:56] Maya: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and an enterprise pack we can share. I'll attach the package to the CRM.
[00:04:03] Priya: great.
[00:04:05] Jordan: regarding benchmarks: after network fix and patched image, we plan a short run: 1) latency microbench for small prompts 2) throughput test with batch sizes matching their workload 3) cold and warm KV cache runs. we'll share the script and the results sheet.
[00:04:20] Liam: sounds good. any blockers to schedule the maintenance window to validate routing?
[00:04:25] Diego: we can do a 2-hour slot next Tuesday, need confirmation.
[00:04:29] Maya: we'll aim for next Tue. I'll follow up in calendar.
[00:04:32] Jordan: on the patched image: note, it requires a minor kernel-module present on the nodes (we added a fallback) — if customers are air-gapped, we provide a tarball and a small install script.
[00:04:43] Liam: we're not fully air-gapped but have strict egress. the tarball + offline install might be easier.
[00:04:50] Jordan: ok i'll include both options in the runbook.
[00:04:53] Diego: on ports, we need to confirm ephemeral ephemeral ranges allowed for gRPC?
[00:04:57] Jordan: we use standard 443 for control and model pull; for internal gRPC we use higher ports but can confine to 15000-16000 if needed, we'll list them.
[00:05:11] Priya: from security side, please confirm audit log encryption at rest and KMS rotations policy.
[00:05:17] Maya: yes we'll document rotation frequency and the option for customer-owned keys.
[00:05:22] [00:30:00] Diego: (later in meeting) ran a small test with Jordan's guidance, after adding static route the TLS handshakes improved but we still see occasional 502s when model fetch is >30s, likely due to idle NAT timeouts.
[00:30:15] Jordan: that matches, increasing the NAT idle timeout and adding sticky route for the control plane should reduce those mid-request failures.
[00:30:25] Liam: agreed. Diego will update TGW propagation to prefer the peering target for the control plane CIDR during the window.
[00:30:32] Diego: yes will do.
[00:30:35] Jordan: we also measured a small regression in p99 for long generations on the patched image, about +8%. we think it's acceptable for pilot but will optimize in the next patch.
[00:30:45] Maya: ok, call to action: Jordan publishes image and allowlist, Maya sends runbook and SOC2 pack, Acme provides route tables and schedules window. We'll reconvene after the validation and benchmark.
[00:30:58] Priya: one more question: any implications for our existing HA model? if we need to fallback to hosted during an incident, how quick is failover?
[00:31:05] Jordan: we support automatic fallback policies; typical failover to hosted endpoints is minutes, depends on DNS TTL and cache. we'll include failover config in the runbook.
[00:31:14] Liam: okay good.
[00:31:16] Maya: thanks everyone, i'll follow up in email with the notes and update CRM. next sync same time next week unless we need an ad-hoc for the maintenance window.
[00:31:25] Diego: thanks.
[00:31:26] Priya: thanks all.
[00:31:27] Jordan: thanks.

Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts (proper nouns sometimes slightly off), follow runbook links for exact commands.
